title: Make website crawling reliable, isolated, and cost-efficient
description:
Replace the fragile crawl orchestration around PR 721 while retaining the native crawler from Alexander. PostgreSQL owns accepted work and lifecycle, ARQ uses an isolated crawler queue, and the product exposes complete stop, retry, scheduling, and failure behavior. Measure embedding input and reuse only exact unchanged work. The detailed review and delivery contract is docs/plans/python-crawler-replacement-review.md.

## Success Criteria

All three reliability and cutover gates pass their behavior and fault tests. Crawls cannot become immortal or block general jobs, unsafe deletion is impossible, users receive complete lifecycle controls, and any later token optimization proves unchanged retrieval quality.
acceptance_criteria: The three delivery gates in the linked plan are complete and validated: durable lifecycle and queue isolation; bounded native-engine correctness with exact embedding accounting; and complete UX, schedules, diagnostics, migration, and cutover. No crawler run can remain immortal, crawler load cannot block general jobs, unsafe deletion is impossible, and optional optimizations do not lower retrieval quality.

title: Establish authoritative crawl lifecycle and isolated execution
description:
First review and rollback boundary on feature/python-crawler. Rebase PR 721, make crawl_runs and attempts the PostgreSQL source of truth for admission, dispatch intent, phases, outcomes, leases, fencing, coalescing, and recovery. Add a dedicated crawler ARQ queue and deployment. Delete the Redis feeder, pending queue, capacity counters, Lua bookkeeping, and crawler work from general workers. Keep crawler admission disabled if this checkpoint is deployed before Gate 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

Accepted work survives Redis loss, worker death, and deployment restart. Dispatch and terminalization are idempotent, admission is fair by tenant and isolated from general jobs, transitions are database-enforced, migrations are recoverable, and feeder machinery is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted work survives Redis loss and deployment restarts; duplicate dispatch and terminalization are harmless; worker death is recovered through an expired lease; one tenant cannot monopolize crawler admission; saturating crawls do not delay representative general jobs; repeated requests for one website coalesce; all transitions are database-enforced; the feeder and its metrics are gone; migrations have preflight, compatibility, and recovery evidence.
close_reason: Gate 1 lifecycle, queue isolation, feeder deletion, expired-delivery convergence, health projection, and crash recovery are implemented and verified.

title: Harden the native crawler and measure indexing cost
description:
Second review boundary. Preserve the native crawler from Alexander while fixing credential and redirect policy, bounded streaming and cancellation, total request budgets, sitemap and validator correctness, per-resource conservation, fenced persistence, parser and file limits, and database-session lifetime. Deepen the existing embedding owners to record exact post-prefix estimated input, retries, provider usage coverage, processing signatures, and a benchmark baseline without changing chunk behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

Zero-page and unreachable runs terminate with typed outcomes; process failure at every phase is recoverable; incomplete observations never delete valid content; every resource is bounded; database transactions do not span provider I/O; and exact embedding inputs, usage coverage, retrieval behavior, CPU, RSS, database, and network baselines are reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: Zero-page and unreachable-site runs reach typed terminal outcomes; process death during fetch, parse, embed, persist, and cleanup cannot create immortal or unsafe work; partial or incomplete observations never delete valid content; memory, disk, requests, pages, files, bytes, and duration are bounded; no database transaction is held across embedding network I/O; exact E5 and non-E5 inputs and usage coverage are tested; the corpus records CPU, RSS, database, network, retrieval, and token baselines; no global vector cache or retrieval-affecting chunk change is introduced.
close_reason: Native crawler reliability and measured performance slice implemented and fully verified; separate schedule work remains deferred.

title: Complete crawl UX, schedules, diagnostics, and cutover
description:
Third review and rollout boundary. Replace frontend string parsing with typed lifecycle fields and actionable localized outcomes. Add stop, try again, coalesced-start feedback, bounded polling, history, next-run visibility, and manual, fixed-interval, or weekday/time/timezone schedules. Add end-to-end diagnostics, version old ARQ payloads, canary the branch, and remove the legacy Scrapy path only after migration evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

Stop and retry work across every nonterminal state, all terminal outcomes stop polling, status is consistent and localized, schedules have deterministic timezone and missed-run behavior without overlap, diagnostics isolate each failure domain, and the canary and rollback envelope are exercised before cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Users can stop pending, queued, and running crawls within a defined bound; retry creates a linked auditable attempt; every terminal outcome stops polling; status is consistent across website and generic job views; Swedish and English copy is localized and safe; schedule DST, missed-run, pause, backoff, and no-overlap behavior is deterministic; diagnostics distinguish API, queue, worker, execution, and remote-site health; canary and schema-compatible rollback are documented and exercised.

title: Reuse exact previous-version embeddings and extracted file text
description:
Optional measured post-cutover tranche. After the Gate 2 baseline and stable operation, persist tenant-scoped processing signatures, exact provider-input digests and token counts, bulk-match only the previous publication, and reuse vectors only after exact text and dimension checks. Distinguish raw file digests from normalized extracted-content digests so metadata-only changes can publish metadata without re-embedding.

## Acceptance Criteria

Only exact tenant-scoped input matches reuse vectors; publication identity, ordering, duplicates, metadata, and citations remain intact; lookup is bounded and bulk; metadata-only file changes skip embedding; submitted input falls on the edit corpus; and retrieval, failure, CPU, RSS, and database guardrails still pass.
acceptance_criteria: Exact unchanged chunks avoid provider submission while new publication rows preserve duplicates, ordinals, ordering, metadata, and citations; model, signature, dimension, text, or tenant mismatch always embeds; lookup is one bounded bulk operation rather than N+1 or pairwise comparison; metadata-only file changes skip embedding; submitted input falls reproducibly on the edit corpus; retrieval behavior, failure semantics, CPU, RSS, and database load remain within agreed guardrails; the optimization can be disabled without changing publication correctness.

title: Decide whether broader crawler caching is earned
description:
Evidence gate, not a commitment to implement. Use production-safe measurements from the reliable crawler and exact previous-version reuse to decide whether a resource manifest, tenant-wide embedding artifacts, different chunk overlap or structure, adaptive scheduling, or another cache layer removes enough measured cost to justify new ownership and cleanup complexity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Record measured benefit, storage and lookup cost, CPU and RSS impact, retrieval results, isolation, lifecycle ownership, and an explicit adopt or reject decision. Cross-tenant vector reuse, silent truncation, and fuzzy or LLM-based skip decisions remain prohibited.
acceptance_criteria: The decision records measured hit rate or avoided network and provider work, storage and lookup cost, CPU and RSS impact, retrieval-quality results, tenant-isolation requirements, lifecycle and deletion ownership, and a clear adopt or reject result. Cross-tenant vector reuse, silent truncation, and fuzzy or LLM-based skip decisions remain prohibited.

title: Bound crawler temporary disk and recover orphaned workspaces
description: PR #721 removes the legacy JSONL spool but downloaded files remain until the entire crawl ends, and a hard worker exit can leave eneo-crawl-* directories on the shared persistent /tmp volume. Make the crawl engine release each downloaded file after its consumer resumes, explicitly close the async event stream on cancellation, isolate crawler-worker temporary storage from upload/export staging, and clean only crawler-owned orphan workspaces before accepting jobs. Do not add a broad /tmp sweeper or change upload/export persistence. Acceptance: normal success, processing failure, cancellation, and worker restart cannot retain crawler-owned files beyond their required lifetime; unrelated /tmp namespaces remain untouched; focused tests, pyright, and touched-file ruff pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified deterministic crawler temp-file release, explicit stream closure, crawler-owned startup recovery, and container-local crawler /tmp isolation.
